reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) directly supports the core mechanistic premise that lattice distortion elevates vacancy formation energy and Al migration barriers, and links this to reduced TGO growth. However, the hypothesis extends beyond the evidence by proposing a specific three-alloy comparison with a control that decouples reactive-element effects, a design not tested in the cited work, and the quantitative prediction of 50-60% reduction is taken from a single MPEA vs. baseline comparison without the proposed control.
premises: Lattice distortion in NiCoCrAl-based MPEAs elevates vacancy formation energy and Al migration barriers in the Al-depletion zone
Suppressed Al diffusion in the ADZ retards growth of non-protective oxides and improves oxidation resistance
A modified MPEA with Y and Hf additions can induce enhanced lattice distortion relative to a baseline NiCoCrAlY
A control alloy with identical Y/Hf but minimal lattice distortion can decouple reactive-element effects from lattice distortion effects
The predicted outcome is a ~50-60% reduction in TGO growth rate for the high-distortion alloy vs. baseline and control
